title: Good coresolutions are exact on cohomology rows
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $M^\bullet,E_0^\bullet,E_1^\bullet,\ldots$ be integer-indexed cochain complexes of abelian groups, with additive differentials $d^n:V^n\to V^{n+1}$ satisfying $d^{n+1}d^n=0$ for each complex $V^\bullet$. Let $u:M^\bullet\to E_0^\bullet$ and $f_i:E_i^\bullet\to E_{i+1}^\bullet$ be chain maps (degree-preserving additive maps commuting with the differentials). Assume $0\to M^\bullet\xrightarrow{u}E_0^\bullet\xrightarrow{f_0}E_1^\bullet\to\cdots$ is exact in every degree. For each $n\in\mathbf Z$ put $C^n(V)=V^n/d_V^{n-1}(V^{n-1})$, and assume the induced sequence $0\to C^n(M)\to C^n(E_0)\to C^n(E_1)\to\cdots$ is exact. Then, writing $H^n(V)=\ker(d_V^n)/d_V^{n-1}(V^{n-1})$, the induced sequence $0\to H^n(M)\xrightarrow{H^n(u)}H^n(E_0)\xrightarrow{H^n(f_0)}H^n(E_1)\to\cdots$ is exact for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. Exactness means that each incoming image equals the following kernel, including injectivity of the first displayed map. No boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Reindex the horizontal sequence by $A_0=M$, $A_{j+1}=E_j$ for $j\ge0$, with maps $h_0=u$, $h_{j+1}=f_j$. Put $A_j=0$ for $j<0$ and let all maps from these zero complexes be zero. The term rows and quotient rows remain exact at every index: at $A_0$ this is precisely the assumed injectivity, and at negative indices it is $0=0$. Chain maps preserve cycles and boundaries since $dh_j=h_jd$, so they induce the displayed maps on $C^n$ and $H^n$. Degreewise exactness gives $h_jh_{j-1}=0$. Consequently the incoming cohomology image is contained in the outgoing kernel.

source.place: Tag 09J0, lemma-good-right-resolution-gives-qis, displayed exact cohomology row; explicit element chase expanding its reference to Tag 09IZ, lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis, first paragraph.

proof.text: Fix $n$. If a cycle $z\in A_0^n$ maps to zero in $H^n(A_1)$, then $h_0z$ is a boundary, so the image of $[z]\in C^n(A_0)$ is zero. Injectivity of $C^n(h_0)$ gives $[z]=0$ in $C^n(A_0)$, that is $z=dy$ for some $y\in A_0^{n-1}$. Its cohomology class is therefore zero. Thus $H^n(h_0)$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 09J0, lemma-good-right-resolution-gives-qis, displayed exact cohomology row; explicit element chase expanding its reference to Tag 09IZ, lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis, first paragraph.

proof.text: Let $j\ge1$ and let a cycle $z\in A_j^n$ represent a class in the kernel of $H^n(h_j)$. Then $h_jz$ is a boundary. Exactness of the $C^n$ row at $A_j$ gives $x\in A_{j-1}^n$ with $[z]=[h_{j-1}x]$. Equality in this quotient means $z=h_{j-1}x+dy$ for some $y\in A_j^{n-1}$. Differentiating and using $dz=d^2y=0$ gives $h_{j-1}dx=0$.

source.place: Tag 09J0, lemma-good-right-resolution-gives-qis, displayed exact cohomology row; explicit element chase expanding its reference to Tag 09IZ, lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis, first paragraph.

proof.text: Exactness of the degree-$(n+1)$ term row at $A_{j-1}$ now gives $t\in A_{j-2}^{n+1}$ such that $dx=h_{j-2}t$. For $j=1$ this says $dx=0$ by injectivity of $h_0$ and takes $t=0$ in $A_{-1}=0$. Since $dx$ is a boundary, $[t]\in C^{n+1}(A_{j-2})$ maps to zero under $C^{n+1}(h_{j-2})$.

source.place: Tag 09J0, lemma-good-right-resolution-gives-qis, displayed exact cohomology row; explicit element chase expanding its reference to Tag 09IZ, lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis, first paragraph.

proof.text: Exactness of the $C^{n+1}$ row at $A_{j-2}$ gives $s\in A_{j-3}^{n+1}$ and $v\in A_{j-2}^n$ with $t=h_{j-3}s+dv$. When $j=1$ take $s=v=0$; when $j=2$, this is exactly injectivity of $C^{n+1}(h_0)$, giving $t=dv$ and $s=0$. Hence $dx=h_{j-2}t=h_{j-2}dv=d(h_{j-2}v)$, using $h_{j-2}h_{j-3}=0$.

source.place: Tag 09J0, lemma-good-right-resolution-gives-qis, displayed exact cohomology row; explicit element chase expanding its reference to Tag 09IZ, lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis, first paragraph.

proof.text: Set $x'=x-h_{j-2}v\in A_{j-1}^n$. The preceding equality gives $dx'=0$, and $h_{j-1}x'=h_{j-1}x$ since $h_{j-1}h_{j-2}=0$. Thus $z=h_{j-1}x'+dy$, so $[z]=H^n(h_{j-1})[x']$. This proves the reverse kernel-image inclusion at every $A_j$, $j\ge1$. Together with step 2 and the inclusion in step 1 it proves the claimed exact cohomology row. The argument used only degrees $n-1,n,n+1$ and finitely many horizontal positions, so it requires no boundedness.

lean.statement: theorem homology_rows_exact (M : CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u} ℤ) (E : ℕ → CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u} ℤ) (u : M ⟶ E 0) (f : ∀ i : ℕ, E i ⟶ E (i + 1)) (h_inj : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Injective (u.f n)) (h₀ : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Exact (u.f n) ((f 0).f n)) (h : ∀ (i : ℕ) (n : ℤ), Function.Exact ((f i).f n) ((f (i + 1)).f n)) (hc_inj : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Injective (opcyclesMap u n)) (hc₀ : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Exact (opcyclesMap u n) (opcyclesMap (f 0) n)) (hc : ∀ (i : ℕ) (n : ℤ), Function.Exact (opcyclesMap (f i) n) (opcyclesMap (f (i + 1)) n)) : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Injective (homologyMap u n) ∧ Function.Exact (homologyMap u n) (homologyMap (f 0) n) ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, Function.Exact (homologyMap (f i) n) (homologyMap (f (i + 1)) n)
